text:
A year after the passing of Archbishop Iakovos of America, a significant memorial event took place in Boston. On April 9, 2006, Professor Athanasios Angelopoulos from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and Nicolas Mottas, a politics graduate from Westminster University in London, attended the first annual memorial service. They represented the Ecumenical Hellenism program and the Institute for National and Religious Studies of Thessalonika.

This event provided an opportunity for Angelopoulos and Mottas to meet with key figures connected to Archbishop Iakovos. They spoke with Nikie Calles, the director of Archbishop Iakovos' archives and his personal secretary for many years, at the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America. Additionally, they met Paulette Poulos, the director of development for Leadership 100 and a former secretary of Iakovos at the Onassis Cultural Centre in New York City. These meetings focused on the unpublished correspondence of the late Archbishop, which deals with human rights and national issues. This ambitious project is set to be published in both Greek and English later this year.

The representatives also had the chance to meet with the current Archbishop of America, Demetrios. The Ecumenical Hellenism program, which began in 1996, has been under the patronage of the Hellenic Republic President Constantinos Stephanopoulos and now operates under the patronage of the Ecumenical Patriarchate and the Church of Greece.

text:
The European Union's competition commission imposed an €899 million (US$1.35 billion) fine on Microsoft, roughly a tenth of its annual revenue. This penalty, the largest ever issued by the EU for an antitrust violation, stems from Microsoft's failure to comply with a 2004 antitrust order.

In 2004, the EU ruled that Microsoft had withheld crucial interoperability information from competitors, hindering their ability to create software compatible with Windows. The commission ordered Microsoft to disclose this information. Microsoft agreed, charging a 6.5% royalty fee on the licensee's product revenues, citing innovation costs (3.87% for the patent license and 2.98% for the information license). The EU deemed these fees unreasonable and ordered Microsoft to reduce them.

Microsoft first lowered the rates to 1.2% (0.7% for the patent license and 0.5% for the information license) within the EU, maintaining the original rate globally. However, the EU still found these rates unreasonable. Two months later, Microsoft further reduced the rates to a flat fee of €10,000 or a 0.4% royalty, applicable worldwide. The EU considered Microsoft's royalty rates during the 15-month period between June 21, 2006, and October 21, 2007, unjustifiably high, leading to the current fine. This brings the total fines imposed on Microsoft in this case to €1.68 billion. The funds will be added to the EU's annual budget.

Microsoft's legal challenges in the EU may not be over. The commission is currently investigating two additional complaints about the company's anti-competitive practices.

The European Union (EU) competitions commission has announced its decision to fine the Microsoft Corporation €899 million (US$1.35 billion), approximately 1/10th of the company's gross yearly earnings, for failing to comply with the 2004 antitrust order. It is the highest ever fine charged by the EU (also being the largest fine of its kind ever imposed upon a company), and the first time that the EU has fined a company because of non-compliance with an antitrust decision.

The first decision in this antitrust case was given in 2004 citing that Microsoft withheld needed interoperability information from rival software companies which prevented them from making software compatible with Windows. Microsoft agreed to this, providing the information for royalty fees of 6.5% of the licensee's revenues for the product on grounds of innovation (specifically, 3.87% for the patent license and of 2.98% for the information license). Microsoft complied with this, adjusting the royalty rates to 1.2% (changing the rates for the licenses to 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively) in the European Union, while keeping the rate the same for the rest of the world. The EU still saw this as an unreasonable rate, and Microsoft, two month after lowering the rates, reduced the rates yet again to a flat rate of €10000 or a royalty of 0.4% applicable worldwide. Microsoft's royalty rates, which were deemed unreasonable for the period of 15 months between June 21, 2006 and October 21, 2007 are the cause for the fine. So far, the EU has fined Microsoft €1.68 billion in 3 separate fines in this case. This fine will go towards the European Union annual budget.

This may not be the end of Microsoft's troubles with the European Union yet, as the commission is currently investigating two other complaints about the company's anti-competition practices.

text:
The book's title, "The Heart of Midlothian," refers to the Old Tolbooth Prison in Edinburgh, Scotland, which was then in the heart of the Scottish county of Midlothian. The story unfolds against the backdrop of the Porteous Riots. In 1736, a riot erupted in Edinburgh over the execution of two smugglers. Captain John Porteous, the Captain of the City Guards, ordered his soldiers to fire into the crowd, killing several people. Porteous was later killed by a lynch mob that stormed the Old Tolbooth.

The main part of the novel is based on a story Scott claimed to have received in an unsigned letter. It was about a woman named Helen Walker who walked all the way to London to seek a royal pardon for her sister, who was wrongly accused of infanticide. Scott replaced Walker with Jeanie Deans, a young woman from a family of highly devout Presbyterians. Jeanie journeys to London, partly on foot, hoping to meet the Queen with the help of the Duke of Argyll. You can find more details about Jeanie Deans' role in the novel in the article about Jeanie Deans (fictional character). Jeanie Deans is the first female protagonist in Scott's works and the first from the lower classes. While she's idealized for her religious devotion and moral rectitude, Scott pokes fun at the moral certitude of the Cameronians, a branch of Presbyterianism represented by Jeanie’s father David.

The novel also delves into early-18th century Jacobitism, a theme common in Scott’s novels. His sympathies shine through in the character of the Duke of Argyll, a moderate on these issues.

"The Heart of Midlothian" has been adapted for the screen once, in 1914, and for television in 1966. Two operas have also been inspired by the novel: "La Prigione di Edimburgo" (Imprisoned in Edinburgh) by Italian composer Federico Ricci (1809–1877) and "Jeanie Deans" by Scottish composer Hamish MacCunn (1868–1916).

A man walking alone near Owhiro Bay quarry car park found an elderly man's body floating in the water. He called the police right away. The victim, believed to be in his 60s, was discovered at 8:30 a.m. NZST.

Police are still figuring out the man's identity and how long his body had been in the water.

text:
In the heart of Washington DC, a man known only as "Mister" disrupts the daily routine of the prestigious law firm Drake & Sweeney. Taking several lawyers hostage, the situation ends tragically when "Mister" is shot by a police sniper. However, the incident leaves a lasting impression on Michael Brock, an antitrust lawyer at the firm. Haunted by what he's learned, Brock embarks on a personal investigation.

His journey leads him to the 14th Street Legal Clinic, where he meets Mordecai Green, a passionate advocate for the homeless. Green invites Brock to volunteer at a homeless shelter, igniting a deeper understanding of the plight of those less fortunate. As Brock delves further, he uncovers a shocking truth: his own firm was involved in an illegal eviction that ultimately resulted in the deaths of a young homeless family.

Grappling with this revelation, Brock makes a drastic decision. He leaves his lucrative position at Drake & Sweeney for a modestly-paid role at the 14th Street Legal Clinic. This choice strains his marriage, leading to a divorce. Yet, amidst these challenges, Brock finds solace in his newfound purpose. He admits a client, Ruby, into a therapy program for drug-addicted women, where he meets Megan, who would become his love interest.

Meanwhile, Drake & Sweeney faces allegations of theft and malpractice from Brock. The Clinic retaliates by filing a lawsuit against the firm and its business partners. Fearing the negative publicity, the case is settled through mediation. The Clinic receives a substantial payout, which is distributed among the eviction's victims.

In a surprising turn, the head partner of Drake & Sweeney, moved by the events, offers pro bono staff to assist the Clinic in its mission. The book concludes with Brock, Megan, and Ruby enjoying a brief vacation, reflecting on their lives and the profound changes they've experienced.

text:
Patients with borderline personality disorder (BPD) often struggle with a disturbed self-image, which is a key symptom of this condition. Evaluations of self-relevance (SR) play a crucial role in cognitive and emotional processing, as well as adaptive behavior.

This study examined whether SR is altered in individuals with higher scores on the Borderline Symptom List (BSL-95) using affective statements. Forty female adults with BPD and 20 healthy participants assessed a series of third-person sentences for their relevance to self.

The results indicated that BPD patients attributed higher SR to negative content compared to healthy controls (p < .001). Additionally, there was a significant positive correlation between the increased bias in evaluating SR of stimuli and borderline symptom severity scores, as measured by the BSL-95 questionnaire (r = 0.67, p < .001). This effect remained significant even after controlling for depressive symptoms through partial correlation analysis.

Our findings demonstrate an enhanced SR for negative statements, which correlates with the severity of individuals’ BPD symptoms. These results contribute to the diagnostic understanding of the disrupted self-organization in this clinical population. We propose that the maladaptive evaluation of SR presents an important target for therapeutic interventions in BPD.

text:
Egypt's leading archaeologist, Zahi Hawass, has unveiled initial ancient artifacts that may guide researchers to the final resting place of Cleopatra and Marc Antony.

Nearby, colorful mummies of nobles were recently unearthed at a neighboring necropolis. These finds suggest that a ruler or person of royalty may be interred within the Temple of Taposiris Magna itself. During the Greco-Roman era, it was common to place tombs of high-ranking officials near those of their rulers.

Dr. Roger Vickers' team used radar to detect three chambers within the rocky hill on which the temple stands. The Temple of Taposiris Magna, dedicated to the goddess Isis, was built around 300 BC by Ptolemy II.

The Supreme Council of Antiquities (SCA) expedition, led by Hawass, has not yet excavated the burial chambers located 40 feet (12 meters) underground. The team hopes to find a crown or Egyptian hieroglyphic cartouches revealing royal names. They plan to use radar again on April 22.

The expedition team includes Hawass, Secretary General of the SCA, and Martinez, who has extensively researched Cleopatra's life.

According to the historian Plutarch, Caesar permitted Marc Antony and Cleopatra to be buried together.

The Temple of Taposiris Magna is situated about 30 miles (48 km) from Alexandria, on a hill along the Mediterranean Sea. The site overlooks the summer residence of Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak. The archaeologists may need to postpone work over the summer due to security concerns.

Severe storms battered Australia's east coast over the past day, causing widespread damage and at least one fatality. Wind gusts reached up to 110 km/h in some areas, leading to flash flooding and power outages from Far North Queensland to Tasmania. Emergency services across the region are overwhelmed, working through the night to respond to the storm's aftermath.

In Far North Queensland, heavy rainfall caused significant issues. Herberton received 60mm of rain in just one hour. Nearby, a couple drove into flooded Sandy Creek, and their car was swept away. The man managed to escape and hold onto a tree, but lost sight of his wife. Rescue teams found the woman on the creek bank later, and fortunately, neither sustained serious injuries. Meanwhile, a search is underway for a missing 38-year-old stockman from Carpentaria Downs Station, who didn't return after checking fences yesterday.

In New South Wales, the State Emergency Service received over 2,300 requests for help, primarily in Western Sydney and Gosford. In Bexley North, three people were rescued from flooded roads, and tragically, a girl died near Mittagong when a tree collapsed onto her tent.

Melbourne experienced severe flooding due to heavy rain and wild storms. The city received 120mm of rain in 24 hours, surpassing the average February rainfall of 45mm and setting a new record for the most rainfall in a day since 1856. Major roads and train lines were disrupted, making travel extremely difficult. A search is ongoing for a schoolboy who may have been swept into floodwaters north of Werribee. Additionally, a 10-year-old girl narrowly avoided being hit by a falling tree in her home and was later rescued and taken to the Royal Children's Hospital in serious condition.

The Spirit of Tasmania I ferry had to return to Port Melbourne after encountering 20-meter waves in the Bass Strait, which broke its windows. Authorities advised residents to avoid Melbourne's city center due to the ongoing hazards.

In a rare event, South Australia experienced hail in February for the first time in 27 years. The storms have caused significant disruptions across the east coast, with emergency services working tirelessly to manage the situation.

text:
The heir to Lord Suth, Carnelian, and Prince Osidian found themselves in a dire predicament. They had been kidnapped, drugged, and spirited away from Osrakum, the capital of the three lands, hidden within funeral urns. Their ordeal began when a grave robber, seeking treasure, chanced upon them. The thief faced a grim choice: report the sighting of the exalted princes and face execution, kill them and risk discovery, or flee with his captives, hoping to sell them into slavery. Desperation drove him to the latter, altering the course of Osidian's planned coronation.

Osidian's absence from the ceremony handed the throne to his brother, Molochite. As the emperor's mortal brother, Osidian was destined to be sacrificed. Bound and disguised, the princes were marched away from the capital, Osidian in worse condition than Carnelian. Carnelian, burdened with the responsibility of their survival, saw an opportunity during an attack by nomad tribesmen. Seizing the moment, he switched their captors, placing them under the tribesmen's custody.

As they journeyed to the ochre tribe's plains, Osidian's health improved. His fearless defense against wild beasts, combined with his navigational prowess—a result of his unique education—and knowledge of the plains, earned the tribesmen's respect. They began to defer to him, recognizing him as a member of the ruling race they had been taught to fear, and as a potential leader to replace their lost chiefs.

Upon reaching the village, Carnelian's quick thinking and the tribesmen's growing respect for Osidian allowed them to live among them. Carnelian adapted to this new life, but Osidian's initial despair turned to vengeful determination. He hatched a plan to reclaim his position, manipulating the tribesmen to his ends. Through a series of staged encounters, he pitted tribesmen from different villages against each other, amassing a growing warband. His ultimate goal: to wage war against his brother and reclaim his rightful place.

text: The Yellow Sarson variety of Brassica rapa exhibits unique yellow seed color genes, which are crucial for developing yellow-seeded cultivars in both B. rapa and B. napus. This study focused on developing near-isogenic lines (NILs) of Yellow Sarson to fine map the major seed coat color QTL SCA9-2 on chromosome A9 and identify candidate genes through linkage mapping and transcriptome sequencing of developing seeds. Linkage analysis and physical mapping within the 18.4 to 22.79 Mb region of SCA9-2 produced six SSR markers with recombination rates ranging from 0.63 to 5.65%. Transcriptome analysis identified 55 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the SCA9-2 region, including three transcription factors: Bra028039 (NAC), Bra023223 (C2H2 type zinc finger), and Bra032362 (TIFY). Additionally, several genes encoding unknown or nucleic acid binding proteins were pinpointed as potential candidates for regulating seed coat color. GO and KEGG enrichment analysis of the DEGs revealed significant enrichment in several biosynthetic pathways, notably flavonoid, phenylpropanoid, and suberin. This research presents the first comprehensive investigation into the yellow seed trait of Yellow Sarson, utilizing linkage mapping and global transcriptome analysis approaches.

Yellow seed is a desirable trait in Brassica oilseed crops. The B. rapa var. Yellow Sarson carry unique yellow seed color genes which are not only important for the development of yellow-seeded oilseed B. rapa cultivars but this variant can also be used to develop yellow-seeded B. napus. Several biosynthetic pathways, including the flavonoid, phenylpropanoid and suberin biosynthetic pathways were significantly enriched through GO and KEGG enrichment analysis of the DEGs. This is the first comprehensive study to understand the yellow seed trait of Yellow Sarson through employing linkage mapping and global transcriptome analysis approaches.

text:
The nuclear war between Nazi Germany and the Race concludes with a German surrender. This turn of events follows the death of Ernst Kaltenbrunner, the Führer, and his replacement by Walter Dornberger. Dornberger quickly agrees to disband the Axis Forces, withdraw German troops from occupied France, and dismantle the German rocket and nuclear programs. The German withdrawal triggers instability among its allies, including the British Union of Fascists, and leads to clashes between the Free French Forces and the new government of liberated France. Additionally, radioactive drift occurs into the Soviet Union.

However, Dornberger secretly begins stockpiling weapons and missile parts, leaving open the possibility for Germany to rearm itself in the future. Meanwhile, the truth behind the nuclear attack on the Race's colony fleet from Second Contact is revealed: it was an American attack, ordered by Earl Warren. Fleetlord Atvar presents Warren with a choice: dismantle the American space program, or allow the Race to nuke Indianapolis as revenge. Surprisingly, Warren chooses to let Indianapolis be destroyed and then commits suicide, handing over control to Vice President Harold Stassen. It later comes to light that Warren prioritized the space program because Americans were developing a starship to reach the Race's homeworld and retaliate for their invasion of Earth.

During this period, the Race faces significant social unrest. The effects of ginger on their females lead to drug addiction, a thriving black market, and prostitution. Their reproductive system, now unregulated, begins to mirror that of humans.

text:
The tour company Barnyard Tours Inc. began with Freddy's idea. The animals agreed and the company launched. They could pay for tours with food or by working for Mr. Bean. However, Freddy and Jinx, the cat, grew weary of leading the tours. Freddy proposed a trip to the North Pole, and he, Jinx, and four other animals set off. A year passed, and those left behind began to worry. Charles, the rooster, gave a speech that sparked a mob in the barnyard.

Ferdinand, a crow from the expedition, returned and organized a rescue party. He reported that the group had taken a ship and the crew planned to eat Freddy. The sailors mentioned they might try to reach Santa Claus’ house. In the woods of Canada, two children and a bear joined the rescue party. However, Ferdinand had forgotten to bring food and clothing. The situation looked grim until he came up with the idea for a lecture tour. The woods' animals contributed food and clothing they had found. Meanwhile, Charles and Jack, a dog, wandered off and were captured by wolves. With the help of some ants, they drove the wolves away. Eventually, they reached Santa Claus’ house.

They found Freddy there but also discovered a problem: the sailors were trying to turn Santa Claus’s irregular workshop into an ordinary assembly line factory. The animals attempted to make the sailors leave by pretending to be ghosts, but one sailor remained unfazed. Freddy then sent the captain, Mr. Hooker, a treasure map, hoping all the sailors would follow him. Instead, Mr. Hooker tried to claim the treasure for himself. Freddy and Jinx chased after him and reclaimed the map. Later, the entire crew saw the map, and the sailors left. Santa Claus’s workshop returned to normal. Santa Claus then took the animals and the two children back to the Bean Farm.

Just before midnight local time on Thursday, Eduardo Rodriguez Veltzé, then President of the Supreme Court of Justice, was sworn in as Bolivia's new president. The country has been mired in a severe crisis for several months.

Earlier that day, the Legislature halted a session in Sucre's House of Liberty, where they had planned to announce the new president of Bolivia. This decision followed intensified protests after it was revealed that a minor had been killed by the Army. Demonstrations also highlighted strong opposition from various social sectors to the potential appointment of either Hormando Vaca Diez, the Senate president, or Mario Cossío, the president of the House of Representatives. Both would have constitutionally succeeded departing president Carlos Mesa, who resigned on Monday night.

Coca leader Evo Morales, a primary opponent of both Mesa and Vaca Diez, had previously backed Rodriguez Veltzé's appointment. While Morales advocates for a constitutional assembly, he may relent if the interim president fulfills his pledge to hold early elections, potentially in December. Meanwhile, Congress is expected to call for parliamentary elections, as the Constitution only mandates that the interim president organize elections for president and vice president.

text:
Armistead Maupin's "Michael Tolliver Lives" marks his comeback to the "Tales of the City" characters after nearly two decades. The seventh installment in the series delves deeper into beloved characters while contrasting the San Francisco of the 1980s, grappling with the AIDS crisis, with the city in the early 2000s. The novel explores aging—both its challenges and joys—and the generational divide between gay men from the 70s and 80s and those from the 2000s.

Breaking from the third-person narrative of the original series, the story is told through Michael Tolliver's first-person perspective. The book opens with Michael reconnecting with an old flame, sparking reflections on his survival through the HIV epidemic—an illness that claimed many of his friends but is now more manageable thanks to advancements in treatment—and the transformed San Francisco shaped by the dot-com boom.

Familiar faces include Anna Madrigal, the former landlady of 28 Barbary Lane; Brian Hawkins and his grown daughter Shawna, a pansexual aspiring writer; and Brian's ex-wife, Mary Ann Singleton. New characters include Michael's younger partner Ben and his transgender coworker Jake Greenleaf. The plot's tension builds around Michael's elderly mother's impending death in Florida, showcasing shifting attitudes since she initially rejected Michael's homosexuality in the second "Tales" book. Additional chapters follow Michael's relationship with his brother Irwin.

Ultimately, Michael faces a difficult choice: be by his mother's side in her final days or support Anna, a figure he considers part of his "logical" family.

So they and four other animals set off. A year passed, and the animals left began to worry. A mob formed in the barnyard triggered by a speech by Charles, the rooster. Everything looked grim for Ferdinand for a minute, but he suddenly came up with the idea for a lecture tour. The animals of the woods brought in food and clothing they found in the woods. They finally arrived at Santa Claus’ house. The animals found Freddy there and also found a problem: The sailors were trying to turn Santa Claus’s irregular workshop into an ordinary, assembly line factory. The animals tried to make the sailors leave. They played ghosts, but one sailor wasn’t scared. Then, Freddy sent the captain, Mr. Hooker, a treasure map. He thought all the sailors would go with him, but instead, he tried to get all of it for himself. Freddy and Jinx chased after him and took it back. Later, the whole crew of the ship was shown the map. The sailors left and Santa Claus’s workshop went back to normal. Santa Claus took the animals and the two children to the Bean Farm.

text:
Egyptian archaeologists have uncovered artifacts that may pinpoint the final resting place of Cleopatra and Marc Antony. The discovery was made outside the Temple of Taposiris Magna, near Alexandria, where colorful mummies of nobles were recently excavated. This finding suggests that a ruler or person of royalty could be buried within the temple itself. During the Greco-Roman era, it was customary to bury high-ranking officials near their rulers.

Dr. Roger Vickers' team used radar to identify three chambers within the rocky hill where the temple stands. The Temple of Taposiris Magna, dedicated to the goddess Isis, was built around 300 BC by Ptolemy II. The Supreme Council of Antiquities (SCA) expedition, led by renowned archaeologist Zahi Hawass, is yet to excavate these burial chambers, located 40 feet (12 meters) underground. They hope to find a crown or Egyptian hieroglyphs known as cartouches that reveal the names of royalty. The team plans to use radar again on April 22.

The SCA expedition includes Hawass, Secretary General of the SCA, and Martinez, who has extensively studied Cleopatra's life. According to the historian Plutarch, Caesar allowed Marc Antony and Cleopatra to be buried together in the same tomb.

The archaeological site is on a hill along the Mediterranean Sea, overlooking the summer home of Egypt's president, Hosni Mubarak. However, the archaeologists may have to postpone their work over the summer months due to security concerns.

text:
A powerful earthquake, measuring magnitude 7.2, hit Japan at 11:46 am local time, roughly 60 miles off the eastern coast of northern Honshu, near Sendai. The quake's force was felt as far away as Tokyo, where buildings swayed and trains were halted as a safety measure. The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center issued a bulletin, and small tsunamis were subsequently observed.

As a precaution, Tohoku Electric's nuclear power plants were shut down. The earthquake caused power outages in Miyagi and Fukushima Prefectures, leaving about 17,000 households without electricity. Railway services, including the Tōhoku Shinkansen, were suspended, and Sendai Airport was temporarily closed.

Fortunately, no deaths have been reported. However, over 69 people across five prefectures were injured, including 26 individuals hurt when a roof collapsed in an indoor swimming pool in Sendai. Additionally, 687 houses in the Tohoku region sustained damage, along with one wooden house in Saitama Prefecture. In this latter incident, a female resident was trapped and rescued after 50 minutes.

text:
After nearly two decades, Armistead Maupin revisits his beloved "Tales of the City" characters in his newest novel. Michael Tolliver Lives picks up where the sixth book left off, delving deeper into the lives of familiar faces and exploring the evolution of San Francisco from the tumultuous 1980s to the dot com boom of the new millennium. The city's transformation, along with the realities of aging—both graceful and distressing—and the generational gap between gays from the 1970s and 80s and those of the 2000s are major themes.

Breaking from the third-person narrative of the original series, the novel is told through Michael Tolliver's first-person perspective. The story begins with Michael bumping into an old flame, sparking reflections on his survival of the HIV epidemic that devastated his peers and the city's radical change. Thanks to advancements in medication, HIV is now manageable, but the memories of the crisis linger.

Alongside Michael, we find Anna Madrigal, the former landlady of 28 Barbary Lane; Brian Hawkins and his grown daughter Shawna, a pansexual aspiring writer; and Brian's ex-wife Mary Ann Singleton. New additions include Ben, Michael's much younger partner, and Jake Greenleaf, a transgender co-worker.

The plot thickens with the impending death of Michael's mother in Florida, highlighting shifts in attitudes since she initially rejected his homosexuality. This subplot intertwines with Michael's relationship with his brother Irwin. As Michael grapples with these challenges, he faces a tough choice: be by his mother's side in her final days or support Anna, a beloved figure now part of his "logical" family.

<source>
 The novel represents Maupin's return to the Tales of the City characters some eighteen years after the sixth book in the series was published. As well as further developing familiar characters, it explores the differences between the San Francisco of the 1980s, bearing the brunt of the developing AIDS crisis, and the city in the first decade of the new millennium. The realities of aging, both distressing and graceful, is a major theme of the book – as well as the generation gap between gays from the 1970s and 80s and gays from the 2000s. In a departure from the third-person style of the original Tales sequence, Michael Tolliver Lives is narrated in the first person by the title character. In the book's opening pages, Michael encounters a half-remembered old flame, prompting him to reflect on his status as a survivor of both the HIV epidemic (which killed many of his peers in the 1980s and 1990s but is now a more treatable chronic illness thanks in part to better medication) and of a San Francisco that has transformed due in large part to the dot com boom. Characters from the original series include Anna Madrigal, the one-time landlady of 28 Barbary Lane; Brian Hawkins and his now-adult daughter Shawna, a pansexual aspiring writer; and Brian's ex-wife Mary Ann Singleton. New characters include Michael's much younger partner Ben and his transgendered co-worker Jake Greenleaf. Much of the plot's tension derives from the impending death of Michael's elderly mother in Florida, a test case of changes in attitude since she refused to accept Michael's homosexuality in the second Tales book. Several chapters involve a secondary plot thread concerning Michael's relationship with his brother Irwin. Eventually Michael finds himself forced to choose between being present for his mother's last days and attending to an aging Anna, described in the book as part of his "logical" (as opposed to "biological") family.
</source>

text:
In 1987, Katy Thatcher, an elderly woman, recounts a pivotal time in her life from 1908 to 1911. Her father was a local doctor, and Katy aspired to follow in his footsteps and become a doctor herself. She became particularly interested in Jacob, a boy known as "touched" from a nearby farm. Jacob couldn't speak but often hummed to himself and seemed to have a unique connection with animals. He would sometimes visit the Thatcher home to be with the animals in the barn. Katy shared Jacob's love for animals and felt she could communicate with him in a basic, empathetic way.

When Jacob's sister, Nell, had a baby out of wedlock with Paul Bishop, Jacob sensed the trouble brewing. One stormy night, he took the baby and brought it to the Thatcher home, hoping to protect it as he had with orphaned lambs. However, his plan didn't unfold as he had hoped.

Later, Katy married Austin Bishop and pursued her dream of becoming a doctor. Fifty years later, the asylum closed, and Jacob was never seen again. There were no records of him being there.

<source>
 The Silent Boy is told by Katy Thatcher, an old woman in 1987, about a critical period in her life from 1908 to 1911. Katy, whose father is a community doctor, dreams of becoming a doctor herself. Katy takes an interest in Jacob, a “touched” boy from a neighboring farm, who can't speak, but somehow hums quietly to himself, and seems able to communicate with animals. Jacob occasionally comes to the Thatcher home to be in the barn with the animals. Katy shares Jacob’s love of animals and comes to feel she can communicate with him in a rudimentary but empathetic way. When Nell, the sister of Jacob, has a baby out of wedlock by Paul Bishop, Jacob is aware of the trouble. He abducts and brings the baby to the Thatcher's house on a stormy night, hoping to save it the way he has saved orphaned lambs by bringing them to a substitute mother. But it doesn't go the way he had planned it to. Later, Katy marries Austin Bishop and becomes a doctor. 50 years later the Asylum closed and Jacob was never seen again. There were no records of him there.
</source>

text:
Addressing the dual epidemic of HIV and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) is a critical public health priority in many sub-Saharan African countries, particularly in those with high HIV burdens such as South Africa. Evidence suggests that poor health due to NCDs and HIV among the workforce increases absenteeism and reduces productivity. However, the prevalence of these coexisting chronic conditions and their associated factors remains unknown among educators. Enhancing our understanding of this issue has important implications for the management and wellbeing of educators. This paper reports the prevalence of selected NCDs and associated factors among HIV-positive educators in South Africa, utilizing data from the 2015/6 survey of Educators in Public Schools in South Africa.

This study was a second-generation surveillance conducted among educators in selected public schools across all nine provinces in South Africa. A multi-stage stratified cluster design with probability proportional to size sampling was employed to draw a random sample of schools. Factors associated with the presence of NCDs were determined using a multivariate backward stepwise logistic regression analysis.

A total of 1,365 schools were sampled, with 21,495 educators (85.5%) participating in interviews. Of the 2,691 HIV-positive educators who responded to questions about NCDs, 36.9% reported having at least one NCD. The most commonly reported NCDs were high blood pressure (17.4%) and stomach ulcers (13.5%). The increased odds of reporting NCDs were significantly associated with being female compared to male [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.5; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.1–1.9; p < 0.002], age 45 to 54 years (aOR = 1.8; 95% CI, 1.4–2.2; p < 0.001), and age 55 years and older compared to those aged 18 to 24 years (aOR = 2.7; 95% CI, 1.8–3.9; p < 0.001). Conversely, the decreased odds of reporting NCDs were significantly associated with not being absent from school for health reasons (aOR = 0.7; 95% CI, 0.6–0.9; p = 0.003).

Integrating NCD care and active screening should be a fundamental component of HIV programs, including prevention, treatment, care, and support interventions among public school educators in South Africa. The education department must invest in health promotion intervention programs to prevent and mitigate the negative impact of NCDs and HIV on the sector.

Nazi Germany and the alien Race ended their nuclear war when the German leader, Ernst Kaltenbrunner, died. His successor, Walter Dornberger, surrendered. He disbanded the Axis Forces, pulled German troops from France, and scrapped Germany's rocket and nuclear programs. This withdrawal shook Germany's allies, like Britain's Fascists, and sparked fights between Free French Forces and the new French government. Radioactive fallout even drifted into the Soviet Union. But Dornberger secretly stashed weapons and missile parts, leaving Germany a path to rearm.

Meanwhile, the Race discovered the Americans, led by Earl Warren, had secretly attacked their colony fleet. Fleetlord Atvar gave Warren a choice: dismantle America's space program or let the Race nuke Indianapolis. Surprisingly, Warren chose the city's destruction over the program, then killed himself. Vice President Harold Stassen took over. Later, it was revealed Warren protected the space program because Americans were building a starship to reach the Race's homeworld.

The Race faced its own chaos. Ginger, introduced by humans, caused social upheaval. Females of the Race became addicted, leading to black markets, prostitution, and uncontrolled reproduction, mimicking human societal issues.

text:
On Epiphany night, Oliver, still wearing his gold paper crown from the kingcake, gazes out his window. Suddenly, a ghostly figure appears in the glass—a boy, a window wraith. Mistaking Oliver for the new king, the wraith urges him to take up a sword and reclaim the kingdom. This mysterious encounter sets Oliver on a journey of self-discovery, one that might just save the world.

The window wraiths, it turns out, are the spirits of France's departed poets and artists, including Molière. They believe Oliver is the king destined to free them from the malevolent force lurking behind the world's mirrors, a force that traps the souls of those who stare too long. The mirrors in the story pay homage to Lewis Carroll's *Through the Looking-Glass*, and there's even a key character descended from Alice Liddell, the real-life inspiration for Carroll's Alice.

text:
Epidural catheters represent the current standard for postoperative analgesia in abdominal surgery. However, due to their potential for neurolysis, they can lead to postoperative urinary tract retention (POUR), necessitating prolonged bladder catheterization and increasing the risk of urinary tract infections (UTIs). Our study aimed to evaluate the current perioperative management of urinary catheters and to determine the optimal timing for suprapubic bladder catheter removal in relation to epidural catheter removal.

We distributed a questionnaire to 102 German hospitals and received responses from 83, which we analyzed to assess the current practices regarding bladder drainage and epidural catheters. Subsequently, we conducted a retrospective study involving 501 patients who had undergone abdominal surgery at the University Hospital Würzburg and received both an epidural and suprapubic catheter. We divided the patients into three groups based on the timing of suprapubic catheter removal relative to epidural catheter removal and evaluated the incidence of UTIs.

Our survey revealed that nearly all hospitals (98.8%) utilize both epidural catheters and bladder drainage post-abdominal surgery. The timing of urinary catheter removal was evenly distributed among the three groups: before, simultaneously with, or after epidural catheter removal (~28–29% for each group). The retrospective study found a 6.7% incidence of catheter-associated UTIs, with women experiencing significantly higher rates than men (10.7% versus 2.5%, p<0.001). There was a non-significant trend suggesting a higher UTI rate when the suprapubic catheter was removed after the epidural catheter (5.7% before, 8.4% after).

The timing of suprapubic bladder drainage removal relative to epidural catheter removal does not appear to correlate with UTI rates. Given the heterogeneous practices observed in Germany, further research is recommended to establish standardized treatment protocols.

text:
This study sought to assess the prevalence of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) and active tuberculosis (TB) within a Colombian prison, alongside investigating intra-prison TB transmission dynamics. Employing a cross-sectional design, the research focused on inmates presenting respiratory symptoms (RS) of any duration, constituting 15% (301/2,020) of the prison population. Of these, 8% were diagnosed with active TB, translating to a prevalence of 1,026 cases per 100,000 inmates, significantly exceeding general population rates.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis was isolated in 79% (19/24) of TB cases, with 94.7% exhibiting susceptibility to first-line drugs. Notably, one isolate demonstrated monoresistance to isoniazid. Genotypic analysis revealed Haarlem as the predominant sub-lineage (68.4%), followed by LAM (26.3%) and T superfamily (5.3%). Molecular genotyping via 24-Locus MIRU-VNTR, both independently and combined with spoligotyping, identified three clusters, each encompassing two isolates. Intriguingly, two clusters involved inmates sharing cells in separate prison blocks, while the third cluster comprised inmates in proximate cells within the same block.

Tuberculin skin testing (TST) was conducted on 95.6% of inmates, with 67.6% yielding positive results. The heightened prevalence of LTBI and active TB within the prison suggests that TB is primarily introduced by inmates or results from endogenous reactivation. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted TB control strategies in carceral settings.

<source>
Active tuberculosis (TB) and latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) are a public health threat in prisons around the world. The objectives of the study were to estimate the prevalence of LTBI and TB as well as to investigate TB transmission inside one prison, in Colombia.

A Cross-sectional study was conducted in inmates who agreed to participate. Inmates with respiratory symptoms (RS) of any duration underwent to medical evaluation and three sputum samples were taken for smear microscopy and culture for TB diagnosis. Drug susceptibility was analyzed using BACTEC MGIT 960 and GenoType MTBDRplus. Molecular genotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates was performed by 24-Locus MIRU-VNTR and spoligotyping. LTBI was evaluated according to the result of the tuberculin skin test (TST). Close contact investigation was conducted inside the prison for inmates that shared the cell with the index TB case.

Among 301/2,020 (15%) inmates with RS of any duration, 8% were diagnosed with active TB. The prevalence of active TB was 1,026 cases/100,000 inmates. We isolated M. tuberculosis in 19/24 (79%) TB cases, 94.7% were susceptible to first line drugs and only one was monoresistant to isoniazid. The most prevalent sub-lineage was Haarlem (68.4%), followed by LAM (26.3%) and T superfamily (5.3%). 24-Locus MIRU-VNTR typing results alone or in combination with spoligotyping identified three clusters containing two isolates each. Two clusters corresponded to inmates that shared the same cell, but each one was located in different blocks of the prison. Inmates from the last cluster were in the same block in nearby cells. TST reading was performed in 95.6% inmates, and 67.6% had a positive reaction.

The prevalence of LTBI and TB was higher in prison than in the general population. Molecular genotyping suggests that TB in this prison is mainly caused by strains imported by inmates or endogenous reactivation.
</source>

On Sunday, an explosion occurred near the Pyramids of Giza in Egypt, according to police reports. The device was reportedly carried by a man from a tourist bazaar, with sources indicating he was transporting the bomb in a sack. It is believed the bomb may have accidentally detonated in the area of Kufr Tuhurmus. The only casualty reported was the bomber himself, Sami Gamal Ahmad, who sustained severe injuries and is unable to be questioned at this time. It is speculated that the man was intending to take the explosive to the tourist area of Kerdassa, where souvenir shops are located near the pyramids, according to an official statement.

These attacks resulted in 88 deaths and left hundreds injured. The current investigation appears to be more focused than the roundup following the October 2004 bombings in the Sinai resorts of Tabas and Ras Shitan, where 3,000 people were detained for questioning. It is reported by Canadian CTV that approximately 200 of those individuals are still in custody.

Among the victims, officials have identified a mix of nationalities, including British, Russian, Dutch, Kuwaiti, Saudi, Qatari, Czech, American, and Egyptian citizens. Sixty of the deceased were identified as Egyptians, with at least eight being foreigners.

The impact of these attacks is already being felt, with tourists abandoning resort hotels and hundreds attempting to leave the country from the nearest international airport.

The bombings took place in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh, with three devices detonating just after 1am. At the Ghazala Gardens hotel, efforts are underway to clear the destroyed reception lobby, where emergency teams have ceased their search for survivors. It is reported that a car laden with 660 pounds of explosives drove into the hotel's driveway and detonated in what appears to be a suicide attack.

The date of the bombings holds significant historical weight for Egypt, marking a national holiday that commemorates the bloodless coup by a group of army officers that led to the deposing of King Farouk in 1952. Egypt has unfortunately experienced 15 tourist attacks since October 1992.

text:
Active tuberculosis (TB) and latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) pose significant public health challenges in prisons globally. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of LTBI and active TB, and to examine TB transmission dynamics within a Colombian prison.

A cross-sectional study was conducted among consenting inmates. Those with respiratory symptoms (RS) of any duration underwent medical evaluation, and three sputum samples were collected for smear microscopy and culture to diagnose TB. Drug susceptibility was assessed using BACTEC MGIT 960 and GenoType MTBDRplus. Molecular genotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates was performed via 24-Locus MIRU-VNTR and spoligotyping. LTBI was evaluated based on tuberculin skin test (TST) results. Additionally, close contact investigations were carried out for inmates sharing cells with index TB cases.

Among 301 inmates (15% of the prison population) reporting RS, 8% were diagnosed with active TB, yielding a prevalence of 1,026 cases per 100,000 inmates. M. tuberculosis was isolated in 19 of 24 (79%) TB cases; 94.7% of these isolates were susceptible to first-line drugs, with only one exhibiting monoresistance to isoniazid. The predominant sub-lineage identified was Haarlem (68.4%), followed by LAM (26.3%) and the T superfamily (5.3%). Molecular genotyping, either alone or combined with spoligotyping, revealed three clusters, each containing two isolates. Two of these clusters involved inmates sharing the same cell but housed in different prison blocks. The third cluster comprised inmates from the same block residing in adjacent cells. TST readings were completed for 95.6% of inmates, with 67.6% exhibiting positive reactions.

The prevalence of LTBI and active TB in this prison exceeded that of the general population. Molecular genotyping suggests that TB within this facility is primarily caused by strains introduced by inmates or through endogenous reactivation.

A tragic discovery was made near the Owhiro Bay quarry car park when a lone walker spotted an elderly man's body floating in the water. The walker promptly contacted the police, who arrived at the scene around 8:30 a.m. NZST. The victim, believed to be in his 60s, was found partially dressed, with both hands severed at the wrists. Investigators also noted signs of an attempted decapitation.

Over 40 officers, including detectives, Wellington Police Maritime, and the Police National Dive Squad, are actively working on the case. They're currently searching for any relevant items and the two missing hands. The victim is described as a European man with grey hair, of moderate build, standing between 175 and 180 centimeters tall. At the time of discovery, he was wearing dark trousers and black leather shoes.

Authorities are still working to identify the man and determine how long his body had been in the water. If you have any information related to this incident, please call the hotline at 0508 Redrocks (0508 733 762).

text:
It's partly autobiographical, focusing on Krish and Ananya, who come from different states—Krish being a Punjabi boy from Delhi, and Ananya a Tamilian from Chennai. They're deeply in love and eager to tie the knot, but it's not going to be easy.

Their story kicks off at IIM Ahmedabad's mess hall, where Krish spots Ananya, the "Best girl of the fresher batch," having a row with the staff about the food. They quickly become friends, hitting the books together every night, and soon, romance blossoms. Both land jobs and start planning their future. First up: convincing the parents.

Krish takes the initiative, winning over Ananya's family one by one. He helps her dad with his first PowerPoint presentation, tutors her brother Manju, and even organizes a concert at his workplace, Citibank, where Ananya's mom gets to sing with T.S. Subramanium and Hariharan—her dream come true.

Meanwhile, Krish's mom's relatives aren't thrilled about him marrying a "Madrasi," but Ananya wins them over by helping one of Krish's cousins find love. With both families now on board, Krish and Ananya arrange a meetup in Goa. But their dream vacation turns into a nightmare when Ananya's parents suspect something fishy between Krish and his mom, leading them to call off the wedding.

Just when all seems lost, Krish's father—who'd previously been more foe than family—steps in. He manages to persuade Ananya's family, giving the couple the green light to finally say "I do." It's a journey filled with humor and cultural jabs at both Tamil and Punjabi traditions, all narrated in the first person.

The tale wraps up with Ananya giving birth to twin boys. The couple muses that their sons belong to a state called 'India,' a nod to ending inequality. And here's a fun fact: Hari, a character from "Five Point Someone," makes a return appearance.

text:
Stress significantly influences the brain and raises the likelihood of developing psychiatric disorders. This impact is mediated through various pathways that alter gene expression and protein function within cells. To grasp how stress exerts such profound effects on the brain, it is essential to understand its stress response pathways. However, previous studies focusing on molecular changes have primarily used repeated or chronic stress models to examine long-term effects, often overlooking integrative genomic and proteomic approaches.

In our study, we investigated the enduring impact of a single stressful event (restraint) on the broad molecular profile of the basolateral amygdala complex (BLC), a critical brain region involved in emotion, memory, and stress. Thirty days post-restraint, we conducted molecular profiling using small RNA sequencing, RNA sequencing, and quantitative mass spectrometry. This approach revealed long-lasting changes in microRNA (miRNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), and proteins. By aligning these three datasets, we identified and validated specific stress-related pathways through qPCR and Western Blot analysis.

Our findings highlight mir-29a-5p as a potential regulator of stress-induced adaptations in the BLC. Additionally, several predicted targets of mir-29a-5p exhibited regulation at both the mRNA and protein levels. The sustained disruption of multiple molecular pathways in the amygdala, triggered by a single stress event, suggests that these changes are sufficient to modify behavioral responses to future experiences, including exposure to additional stressors.

text: Marine vertebrates, such as seabirds and pinnipeds, significantly contribute to biogeochemical processes by transporting nutrients from marine to terrestrial ecosystems. Soils enriched with animal deposits typically exhibit elevated levels of organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus. While numerous studies have explored bacterial diversity in Antarctic soils influenced by marine animals, many have been conducted in areas with substantial human activity. To address this, we selected Cape Shirreff, Livingston Island, an Antarctic Specially Protected Area with minimal human impact, as our study site. We chose sampling locations with varying cohabiting animal species within a limited area to assess the impact of animal concentrations on soil bacterial diversity and composition via their influence on edaphic characteristics. Utilizing 16S rRNA gene sequencing, we found that soils influenced by Antarctic fur seals and kelp gulls exhibited nutrient compositions more akin to control soils (those devoid of visible plant or animal presence). This similarity may stem from the comparatively active behavior of these species. In contrast, soils from southern elephant seal and penguin concentrations displayed marked nutrient composition differences relative to controls. Correspondingly, bacterial communities in these soils diverged most significantly from control soils, with penguin colony soils demonstrating the lowest bacterial diversity. The European Union's competition commission slapped Microsoft with an €899 million (US$1.35 billion) fine for violating a 2004 antitrust order. This penalty, equivalent to about one-tenth of Microsoft's yearly earnings, marks the EU's largest-ever fine of this kind and its first fine for non-compliance with an antitrust decision.

Carnelian, heir to Lord Suth, and Prince Osidian were snatched, drugged, and secretly spirited out of Osrakum, the capital of the three lands, hidden within funeral urns. Carnelian's awakening was prompted by a grave robber rummaging through the urns, seeking plunder. The thief found himself in a dire predicament: he had gazed upon the face of one of the chosen lords, a crime punishable by death. His options were grim—kill the captives and risk eventual discovery, be caught during the inevitable hunt for the missing nobles and executed, or flee with his captives, hoping to sell them as slaves. Desperate, he chose the latter, altering the course of Carnelian and Osidian's lives forever.

Osidian's absence from his coronation led to an unforeseen consequence: his brother Molochite would assume the throne, and Osidian, as the new emperor's mortal brother, would be sacrificed. Bound and disguised, the two were marched away from the capital, with Osidian in worse condition than Carnelian. Carnelian faced a tough choice: attempt an escape, but leaving Osidian behind or bringing him back would seal Osidian's fate. Instead, he seized an opportunity during a nomad tribesmen attack, transferring their captivity to the tribesmen.

As they journeyed back to the ochre tribe's plains, Osidian began to recover. His reckless bravery in defending the party from wild animals, along with his navigational skills and knowledge of the plains—gained from his privileged education—impressed the tribesmen. They started to defer to him, recognizing him as a member of the ruling race they feared and a natural leader to replace their fallen chiefs.

Upon arriving at the village, Carnelian's quick thinking and the tribesmen's growing respect for Osidian allowed them to live among the village. Carnelian accepted their new life, but Osidian initially struggled, his despair turning into vengeful determination. He devised a plan to reclaim his position, manipulating the tribesmen to his will. Through a series of staged encounters, he pitted tribesmen from different villages against each other, steadily growing his warband. His ultimate goal? To forge an army and wage war against his brother, the new emperor.

text:
Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is marked by a disturbed self-image, which plays a crucial role in cognitive and emotional processing and adaptive behavior. In this study, we examined whether self-relevance (SR) evaluations are altered in individuals with higher BPD symptom scores, using affective statements as stimuli.

Forty female adults with BPD and 20 healthy controls assessed sentences in the third person for their relevance to the self. BPD patients showed a heightened SR for negative content compared to healthy controls (p < .001). Additionally, we found a significant positive correlation between the increased bias in SR evaluations and BPD symptom severity, as measured by the Borderline Symptom List-95 (BSL-95) questionnaire (r = 0.67, p < .001). This relationship remained significant even after accounting for depressive symptoms through partial correlation analysis.

Our findings indicate an enhanced SR for negative statements in BPD, which correlates with the severity of BPD symptoms. These results contribute to our understanding of the disrupted self-organization in BPD and suggest that maladaptive SR evaluations could be a valuable target for BPD treatment approaches.

text: The protagonist of The Sun Also Rises is Jake Barnes, an expatriate American journalist living in Paris. Jake suffered a war wound that has caused him to be impotent; the nature of his injury is not explicitly described in the novel. He is in love with Lady Brett Ashley, a twice-divorced Englishwoman. Brett, with her bobbed hair, embodies the new sexual freedom of the 1920s, having had numerous love affairs. Book One is set in the Café society of Paris. In the opening scenes, Jake plays tennis with his college friend Robert Cohn, picks up a prostitute (Georgette), and runs into Brett and Count Mippipopolous in a nightclub. Brett and Jake leave together; in a taxi she tells him she loves him, but they know they have no chance at a lasting relationship. In Book Two Jake is joined by Bill Gorton, recently arrived from New York, and Brett's fiancé Mike Campbell, who arrives from Scotland. Jake and Bill travel to Spain, where they meet Robert Cohn north of Pamplona for a fishing trip. Cohn, however, leaves for Pamplona to wait for Brett and Mike. Cohn had an affair with Brett a few weeks earlier and still feels possessive of her despite her engagement to Mike. Jake and Bill enjoy five days of tranquility, fishing the streams near Burguete, after which they rejoin the group in Pamplona, where they begin to drink heavily. Cohn's presence is increasingly resented by the others, who taunt him with anti-semitic remarks. During the fiesta the characters drink, eat, watch the running of the bulls, attend bullfights, and bicker with each other. Jake introduces Brett to Romero at Montoya's hotel; she is smitten with the 19-year-old matador and seduces him. The jealous tension among the men builds; Jake, Campbell, Cohn, and Romero each love Brett. Cohn, who had been a champion boxer in college, has fistfights with Jake, Mike, and Romero, whom he injures. Despite the tension, Romero continues to perform brilliantly in the bullring. Book Three shows the characters in the aftermath of the fiesta. Sober again, they leave Pamplona. Bill returns to Paris, Mike stays in Bayonne, and Jake goes to San Sebastián in northeastern Spain. As Jake is about to return to Paris, he receives a telegram from Brett asking for help; she had left with Romero for Madrid. He finds her in a cheap hotel, without money, and without Romero. She announces she has decided to go back to Mike. The novel ends with Jake and Brett in a taxi speaking of the things that might have been.

text: This novel portrays a love affair between Jadine and Son, two Black Americans from very different worlds. Jadine is a beautiful Sorbonne graduate and fashion model who has been sponsored into wealth and privilege by the Streets, a wealthy white family who employ Jadine's aunt and uncle as domestic servants. Son is an impoverished, strong-minded man who washes up at the Streets' estate on a Caribbean island. As Jadine and Son come together, their affair ruptures the illusions and self-deceptions that held together the world and relationships at the estate. They travel back to the U.S. to search for somewhere they can both be at home, and find that their homes hold poison for each other. The struggle of Jadine and Son reveals the pain, struggle, and compromises confronting Black Americans seeking to live and love with integrity in the United States.

After a detective found out about Henri Kanarack, Osborn plans to kill him. He shoots Kanarack and the last information Osborn could get from Kanarack was that he was murdering Osborn's father for hire of Erwin Scholl. Osborn tells McVey about Scholl. Out of McVey's researches arises that Osborn's father invented a scalpel that can be used at degrees of absolute zero and that in the same year he was killed a few other inventors were killed, whose inventions were all about surgery at extremely high or low temperatures and all vanished. Because of that McVey and his investigation team have a suspicion that Scholl and his people might belong to an organization that's working on surgery making it possible to combine deep-frozen body parts and to thaw it so the person is alive. Time passes, and McVey finds out about Elton Lybarger and a ceremony that should be held in Berlin. During this in the main hall of the building Elton Lybarger is giving the speech. After Osborn followed Von Holden, the only remaining organization member, to Switzerland and is nearly killed McVey gives Osborn a VCR tape, on which Osborn finds a whole confession of Elton Lybarger's physician. He confesses having experienced the surgery on Lybarger, because they were searching for a person, whose attributes and fingerprints were as much as the same as Adolf Hitler's, and having helped the organization, who was trying to build a new third Reich, to raise Lybarger's two “nephews”, the perfect Aryans, who were raised with him since they were young. He sees how Van holden falls into a crevasse and how he opens the package Von Holden had been carrying with him all the time, and it's the deep-frozen head of Adolf Hitler.

text: A young girl called Lila wants to become a firework-maker, like her father Lalchand. Despite her talents, Lalchand believes this is an unsuitable job for girls. Lila disagrees, and journeys to get Royal Sulphur from Razvani the Fire-Fiend at Mount Merapi, as all aspirant firework-makers must do. The quest is nearly unsuccessful, as she does not have protection from the Fire-Fiend's flames or the Three Gifts to present to Razvani. However, her friends Hamlet, a talking white elephant, and Chulak, Hamlet's caretaker, manage to deliver the water of the Goddess of the Emerald Lake that will protect her. To Lila's surprise, Razvani recognizes her as a firework maker who has brought the Three Gifts, despite Lila being unaware of what the Three Gifts are. Upon her return home, she learns that Lalchand has been imprisoned for the disappearance of Hamlet. To save his life, Lila and Lalchand must win the upcoming competition for the Firework Festival against other extremely talented firework makers. Upon their victory, Lalchand explains to his daughter that she does possess the Three Gifts: rather than tangible objects, they are talent, courage, and luck, all of which she has. She has talent, having worked with her father at firework-making for many years; courage, for having undertaken the journey; and good fortune, which lies in having loyal friends, Chulak and Hamlet.

text: Gwynedd in north Wales is ruled by Math, son of Mathonwy, whose feet must be held by a virgin at all times except while he is at war. Math's nephew Gilfaethwy is in love with Goewin, the current footholder, and Gilfaethwy's brother Gwydion tricks Math into going to war against Pryderi so Gilfaethwy can have access to her. Gwydion kills Pryderi, Prince of Dyfed, in single combat, and Gilfaethwy rapes Goewin. Math marries Goewin in compensation for her rape, and banishes Gwydion and Gilfaethwy, transforming them into a breeding pair of deer, then pigs, then wolves. After three years they are restored to human form and return. Math needs a new footholder, and Gwydion suggests his sister, Arianrhod, but when Math magically tests her virginity, she gives birth to two sons. One, Dylan, immediately takes to the sea. The other is raised by Gwydion, but Arianrhod swears that he will never have a name or arms unless she gives them to him, and refuses to do so. Gwydion tricks her into naming him Llew Llaw Gyffes (Llew Skilful Hand) and giving him arms. She then swears he will never have a wife of any race living on earth, so Gwydion and Math make him a beautiful wife from flowers, and name her Blodeuwedd ("Flowers"). Blodeuwedd falls in love with a passing hunter called Goronwy, and they plot to kill Llew. Blodewedd tricks Llew into revealing the means by which he can be killed, but when Goronwy attempts to do the deed, Llew escapes, though wounded, transformed into an eagle. Gwydion finds Llew and transforms him back into human form, and turns Blodeuwedd into an owl (Blodeuwedd, literally "Flower Face," means "Owl"). Goronwy offers to compensate Llew, but Llew insists on returning the blow that was struck against him. He kills Goronwy with his spear, which is thrown so hard it pierces him through the stone he is hiding behind.

Caffery is convinced the attacker will be targeting another family and when Rory's body is discovered and DNA from semen proves to be Rory's father Alek, the case is turned on its head. Bite marks on the boy's shoulder, however, do not match Alek's dental pattern and Caffery then understands that Peach was forced to sodomise his son. Another family with a young boy, 8-year-old Josh, has been imprisoned and Caffery slowly pieces together the clues to find out who they are. Caffery also gets very close to discovering that his brother is still alive. He suffered brain damage at the hands of a vicious child molester, a member of a paedophile ring who hand children round and make child pornography videos.

text: Benjamin is born with the physical appearance of a 70-year-old man, already able to speak. His father Roger invites neighborhood boys to play with him and orders him to play with children's toys, but Benjamin only obeys to please his father. At five, Benjamin is sent to kindergarten but is quickly withdrawn after he repeatedly falls asleep during child activities. When Benjamin turns 12, the Button family realizes that he is aging backward. At the age of 18, Benjamin enrolls in Yale College but having run out of hair dye on the day of registration, is sent home by officials, who think he is a 50-year-old lunatic. In 1880, Benjamin is 20, his father gives him a control of Roger Button & Co. Wholesale Hardware. He meets Hildegarde Moncrief, a daughter of General Moncrief, and falls in love with her at the first sight. Hildegarde mistakes Benjamin for a 50-year old younger brother of Roger Button, and without realizing the fact of Benjamin's abnormality, the two get married six months later. Years later, Benjamin's business has been a great success, but his family life hasn't been well for him. Benjamin starts to get tired of Hildegarde because she's a nagging woman that is no longer beautiful as before. His family life is so boring that he joins the Spanish-American War in 1898. He had a great success in the military, ranked up to lieutenant colonel, and rewarded with a medal. He then quits the military because his company requires his care. In 1910, Benjamin turns over control of his company to his son, Roscoe, and enrolls at Harvard University, having the appearance of a twenty-year-old. His first year at Harvard is a great success, and he is dominant in American football, notably obtaining revenge against Yale for his earlier unpleasant experience. However, by the time Benjamin reaches his last 2 years, he is a weak sixteen-year-old, unable to play football and barely able to cope with the academic load. After graduation, Benjamin returns home, only to learn his wife has moved to Italy. He lives with Roscoe, who treats him very sternly, making Benjamin call him "Uncle" in front of his house guests. As the years progress, Benjamin turns from a moody teenager into a young child. Eventually Roscoe has a child that later attends kindergarten with Benjamin. After kindergarten, Benjamin slowly begins to lose memory of his earlier life. His memory fades away to the point where he cannot remember anything except his nurse. Then everything fades to darkness.

text: Mr. and Mrs. Edward Brookenham host an effete, rather corrupt social circle. They are the parents of worthless Harold and sweet but knowledgeable Nanda (age eighteen). Mr. Longdon attends one of their social functions and is amazed at how much Nanda resembles her grandmother, his long-ago love who married another man. Vanderbank, a young civil servant with little money, admires both Mrs. Brookenham (nicknamed "Mrs. Brook") and Nanda. Mrs. Brook seems to want an affair with "Van" but he appears more interested in Nanda. Mr. Longdon promises him a dowry if he marries Nanda. Mrs. Brook is instead trying to get her daughter married to Mitchy, a very rich but rather naive member of her social circle. text: Prior to the events The Phantom Menace, Palpatine politically manipulates his colleagues in the Galactic Senate, especially supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum. As the Sith Lord Darth Sidious, he begins to slowly put the Neimoidians and the Trade Federation in position for his blockade of Naboo. A terrorist group named the Nebula Front threatens the activities of the Trade Federation. They are protesting the actions of the Federation and will resort to any means necessary to disrupt the Trade Federation. They hire Captain Cohl to carry out terrorist acts against their business. However, Jedi Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi are hot on the trail of the terrorists and thwart their plans. The Trade Federation petitions the Senate to allow them to increase their number of droid fighters, battle droids, and other defenses. Valorum considers this, but on advice from Palpatine he demands that in exchange the Republic be allowed to tax some of the trade routes they hold. This sparks a debate and a summit is scheduled to be held on the matter. Taking extreme measures, the Nebula Front sets plans in motion to assassinate Valorum at the summit to prevent the taxation. The Jedi Council, along with Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan, step in to track down Captain Cohl and the would-be assassins. While writing the novel, James Luceno was granted access to parts of the screenplay drafts and concept art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones. As such, Cloak of Deception was the first (real life) appearance of almost all of the new characters and organizations from Attack of the Clones, including the Techno Union, Passel Argente, and other Separatists. At the end of chapter 29 the word 'thought' is missing the 't' at the end. In chapter 33, the word 'a' is incorrectly written as 'an'. Opening crawl After a thousand generations of peace, the Galactic Republic is crumbling. On Coruscant, at the center of civilized space, greed and corruption riddle the Senate, beyond even the abilities of Supreme Chancellor Valorum to remedy. And in the outlying systems, the Trade Federation dominates the hyperlanes with its gargantuan vessels. But now even the Trade Federation finds itself assailed from all quarters, preyed upon by pirates and raiders, and victimized by terrorists, who demand an end to the Federation's tyrannical practices. It is a time that tests the mettle of all those who strive to hold the Republic together—none more than the Jedi Knights, who have long been the Republic's best hope for preserving peace and justice…

text: The novel is set in early 20th century India in the estate of the Bengali zamindar Nikhil. He marries Bimala, a woman who is both of a lower status and of a darker complexion, which is contradictory to his family traditions. Their love is idyllic and both are dedicated to one another until the appearance of his friend and radical revolutionist, Sandip. Sandip, a passionate and active man, is a contradiction to the peace-loving and somewhat passive Nikhil. His charismatic speech, support of the Swadeshi movement, and a renewed appreciation of everything Indian while denying everything British garnered support from local natives across the province. After hearing Sandip speak at a rally, Bimala insists that Sandip visit Nikhil’s estate. While visiting, Sandip's influential nature easily attracts the innocent and unsuspecting Bimala, and she suggests he make his headquarters at their house. Once empowered by the inside world, knowing only her husband and home, she becomes engaged with the outside world, taking part in the Swadeshi movement by working with Sandip. As the novel develops, Bimala is drawn to Sandip’s passion and the attraction between the two becomes inevitable, producing a love triangle. She begins to question her marriage with Nikhil and finds in Sandip what she has always sought after in a man: zeal, ambition, and a hint of danger. She begins to help Sandip by stealing money from Nikhil’s treasury, convinced that if it is not equally his money as well as hers, then it belongs to the country. While Bimala claims her national duty as motivation, her true intentions lie in pleasing Sandip. Nikhil subsequently discovers their actions, but grants Bimala freedom to grow and choose what she wants in her life (as their marriage was arranged when she was a young girl). Meanwhile, Bimala experiences love for the first time, which ultimately helps her understand that it is indeed her husband Nikhil who really loves her. The novel ends with a riot, resulting in Sandip fleeing the city. Nikhil is mortally wounded in the head. Amulya, a young follower of Sandip's movement who considered Bimala as his sister, and whom Bimala thinks of as her son (since she has no children), dies by a bullet through his heart.

text:
Tattooing especially gains popularity among both men and women in adulthood from the wide range of socioeconomic groups and is noted as a risk taking behaviour in adults. Especially when tattooing does not perform to the highest standards, it can potentially be the hazardous practice. Myanmar has a paucity of evidence-based information on the estimated prevalence of tattoos and awareness of potential disease transmission from tattooing under insanitary conditions as well as the infection risk. The present research was undertaken to help identify the self-reported prevalence of tattooing among adults (18–35 years) and their knowledge of transmission risk of blood-borne infections and its determinants.

A community-based cross-sectional study focused on residents aged 18–35 years was carried out in two urban and two rural areas in Mandalay district, Mandalay Region during 2015. Trained interviewers used a pre-tested structured questionnaire for face-to-face interviews with one eligible participant per selected household (n = 401). Bivariate analysis and multivariable analysis using binary logistic regression were done to ascertain the relevant explanatory variables.

The overall self-reported prevalence of tattooing was 19.5% (78/401) (95% CI = 16–24). Nearly 80% of participants (318/401) knew at least one blood-borne viral infection that could be transmitted from tattooing. The persons who had high formal education, manual laborers and those who lived with their families were significantly more likely to cite at least one blood-borne viral infection. Their perceived possibility to remove tattoo independently influenced the practice of tattooing (aOR = 1.91, 95% CI = 1.06–3.45; p = 0.03) compared with participants who reported no perceived possibility. Tattooing was more common in male (aOR = 13.07, 95% CI = 6.25–27.33; p<0.001) compared to female which was independently significant.

This study ascertained the tattoo prevalence as two in ten adults of working age especially among male in central part of Myanmar in the context of lack of registration system for tattoo parlours and the issuance of safety guidelines. Findings have suggested the target groups and risk factors to be included in future health promotion programs. Future research directions should focus on perspectives of tattooists to create and sustain the sanitary practices to reduce the chance of transmission of blood-borne viral infections.

text: Antarctica is often associated with images of masculine figures battling against the blizzard. The pervasiveness of heroic white masculine leadership and exploration in Antarctica and, more broadly, in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, and Medicine (STEMM) research cultures, has meant women have had lesser access to Antarctic research and fieldwork opportunities, with a marked increase since the 1980s. This article presents findings from an exploratory online survey examining how 95 women experienced research and remote Antarctic fieldwork with the Australian Antarctic Program. Although women are entering polar science in greater numbers, a key theme of the qualitative findings of this survey is that gendered barriers to participation in research and fieldwork persist. We discuss five key gendered barriers including: 1) Physical barriers, 2) Caring responsibilities/unpaid work, 3) Cultural sexism/gender bias, 4) Lack of opportunities/recognition, and 5) Unwanted male attention/sexual harassment. We argue that the lack of attention paid to gender and sexuality in polar fieldwork contributes to the invisibility and exclusion of women and other marginalized identities broadly. To conclude, we point to the importance of targeted inclusivity, diversity and equity initiatives through Antarctic research globally and specifically by National Antarctic Programs.
